CHN.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Treat the 1 August List 4 announcement as a breach of the Osaka ceasefire and complete a proportional, already-signaled response: keep the 5 August halt on U.S. farm purchases in force, prepare additional tariffs on remaining U.S. goods if the 10% duties on ~$300B take effect on 1 September, and hold the unreliable-entity and rare-earth options in reserve rather than firing them now. Keep the early-September Washington talks open, but do not offer new purchase or structural concessions while Huawei remains fully Entity-Listed and the manipulator designation stands. Do not push a disorderly yuan slide or a Treasury dump; those would add capital-outflow and financial-stability risk on top of the tariff shock.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is high, not existential. Combined U.S. coverage is moving from ~$250B at 25% (List 3 hike, 10 May) to essentially all remaining Chinese goods at 10% from 1 September (1 August announcement), after Shanghai talks produced little progress (30–31 July) and after the Osaka pledge of no new tariffs “for the time being” (29 June). The May Entity List plus Google/chip cutoffs is a firm-level strike on Huawei’s global smartphone and 5G position; the temporary general license expires 19 August. Macro already shows the bite: China industrial production slowed from 108.5 to 104.4 (Mar–Aug), merchandise exports fell about 5.6% in the window, and USD/CNY broke 7 (7.0592 on 7 August) for the first time since 2008, prompting the first U.S. manipulator designation since 1994. Reserves remain ~$3.13T and IP is still expanding, so this is not a financial-stability emergency — hence +0.55, not +1.0. Action should be retaliate, not concede and not maximal escalate: MOFCOM/Xinhua already framed List 4 as a “serious violation” of the Xi–Trump consensus and suspended farm buying (a direct hit on a politically sensitive U.S. sector that had already collapsed from $19.5B in 2017 to $9.1B in 2018). Further non-tariff nuclear options (rare-earth cutoff, full unreliable-entity implementation, unmanaged devaluation) would invite a List 4 hike toward 25% and more Entity-List spillover while risking outflows now that the 7 floor is gone. A calibrated farm/tariff mirror keeps leverage into September talks without converting a high export-and-tech threat into an FX-and-legitimacy crisis.
key_factors: List 4 10% on remaining ~$300B announced 1 Aug, effective 1 Sep, after Osaka no-new-tariffs pledge
Huawei Entity List plus Google/Android and U.S. chip cutoff; TGL expires 19 Aug
USD/CNY broke 7; U.S. manipulator designation 5 Aug (first since 1994)
China IP slowing (108.5 to 104.4) and SA exports down ~5.6%; reserves still ~$3.13T
MOFCOM already halted U.S. farm purchases and left room for more ag tariffs
U.S. also showing stress (UMCSENT 89.8, 10Y 1.71, VIX spike) so leverage exists without going nuclear

sources_cited.excerpt: After the Shanghai round, Trump announces 10% tariffs on the remaining ~$300B of Chinese goods (List 4), effective Sept 1.
After CNY breaks 7 per USD, US Treasury designates China a currency manipulator (first such designation since 1994).
US Commerce Department adds Huawei and affiliates to the Entity List. US firms generally barred from selling to Huawei without a license.
G20 Osaka: Trump and Xi agree to resume talks. Existing tariffs remain; no new tariffs "for the time being."
List 3 tariff rate rises from 10% to 25%.
China industrial production index (same period previous year=100) slowed from 108.5 (2019-03) to 104.4 (2019-08).
China SA merchandise exports fell from $218.96B (2019-03) to $206.61B (2019-08), about -5.6%.
USD/CNY rose from 6.79 in mid-February to 7.0592 on 2019-08-07 after breaking 7 on 2019-08-05.
China reserves excluding gold remained stable near $3.13T (latest $3,126.4B on 2019-08-01).
China has halted its purchases of U.S. agricultural products and will not rule out levying import tariffs on American farm imports purchased after Aug. 3.
Trump’s new 10% tariff on $300B was “a serious violation of the consensus of the heads of state”; related Chinese companies suspended purchasing U.S. agricultural products.
Google suspended Android/GMS licensing and U.S. chip suppliers paused sales after the Entity List — described as a potential kill switch for Huawei’s global smartphone ambitions.
